fields.title: Polka: the assistant that makes things up
fields.summary: 340 "inaccurate" marks in a month. The model lists ingredients that are not in the description.
fields.decisionPrompt: What do we do? Name the price of your solution.
fields.brief/role: You are the PM for Polka.
fields.brief/company: Polka is a fictional grocery delivery service from local stores: 900 partner stores, a buyer app, and a partner dashboard.
fields.brief/context: You are the PM for Polka. The "ask about a product" feature launched a month ago. Over the month, 41 thousand answers, 340 "inaccurate" marks. Breakdown of marks: 120 — the model named ingredients not in the description; 90 — answers to medical questions; 70 — contradictory answers to the same question; 60 — other.
fields.brief/objective: Remove the errors caused by our task formulation rather than the model.
fields.brief/constraints: A stronger model costs twice as much and takes three days to switch.
fields.brief/task: Decide what you do and name which errors will remain.
fields.learnTakeaway/title: A stronger model does not mean fewer hallucinations
fields.learnTakeaway/body: When data is missing, the model fills the gap with plausible text, and a more expensive one does it more convincingly. Therefore, you first categorize errors by cause: what is missing from the data, what is missing from the instruction, and what causes variance. Cheap fixes close most issues, and the rest are cured by verifiability — an answer that shows its source leaves no room for argument.
fields.evidenceCards/0/content: Prompt: 380-token instruction, product description from the catalog, question. Default temperature. No format specified.
fields.evidenceCards/1/content: Ingredients specified for 62% of products, allergens for 41%.
fields.evidenceCards/2/content: "You are a grocery store assistant. Answer customer questions about products using the description. Be helpful and friendly."
fields.evidenceCards/3/content: "A stronger model is twice as expensive, 3 days to switch. Instruction tweaks — hours. Strict format with a source quote — 3 days. Temperature — minutes."
fields.decisionOptions/0/description: Switch to a stronger model. 3 days, twice as expensive.
fields.decisionOptions/0/consequence: wording quality will improve. Solves none of the four problems: ingredients missing from data, medical questions not forbidden by instruction, format not specified, high temperature.
fields.decisionOptions/1/label: Rewrite the instruction and lower the temperature
fields.decisionOptions/1/description: Rewrite the instruction and lower the temperature. Hours.
fields.decisionOptions/1/consequence: closes medical questions, allows answering "not specified", sets format and tone, reduces contradictions. The cheapest option, addresses three of the four groups. Does not provide verifiability.
fields.decisionOptions/2/label: Instruction plus strict format with an ingredient quote
fields.decisionOptions/2/description: Instruction plus strict format with an ingredient quote. 3 days.
fields.decisionOptions/2/consequence: everything from B plus verifiability: the answer contains a quote from the source. Experience shows this reduces both the number of errors and arguments about them.
fields.decisionOptions/3/description: Disable the feature until investigation. Immediately.
fields.decisionOptions/3/consequence: completely closes the legal risk. Loses a feature whose users have 12% higher conversion. 0.8% "inaccurate" marks is not a scale that justifies disabling.
fields.rubric/remediation/0/gap: Does not analyze the cause of poor answers sequentially
fields.rubric/remediation/1/gap: Does not connect variance to temperature and format
fields.rubric/remediation/2/gap: Does not use the source as a trust mechanism
fields.rubric/remediation/3/gap: Context window and prompt contents are not considered a source of errors
